verdict.summary: Accessing remains technically close to RC quality, with strong product definition, Symfony-oriented architecture, authentication capabilities, documentation, and QA tooling, but the assessed state is still an untagged refactor branch with a dirty working tree and a transitional gating migration.
strengths: Authentication and identity responsibilities are explicitly documented through product, architecture, bounding, audit, market, and full manifests.
The runtime baseline is modern and substantial, using PHP 8.4, Symfony 8.1, Doctrine ORM, Security, WebAuthn, OTP, rate limiting, serializer, validator, mailer, and notifier capabilities.
QA infrastructure includes PHPUnit 12, PHPStan 2.1, PHP CS Fixer, coverage tooling, Panther, and Playwright.
Recent commits show active security-test expansion, schema-parity hardening, dependency alignment, and PHPUnit coverage-tooling work.
CI/workflow, deployment, documentation, and gating assets are materially present.
risks: The assessed HEAD is on refactor/accessing-canonical-structure rather than an immutable tagged RC.
The working tree is not clean because tracked gating configuration is deleted while a substantial replacement gating tree is untracked.
The transitional gating state reduces reproducibility and prevents treating the current snapshot as a finalized release baseline.
The supplied facts describe available quality tooling but do not include successful results from the complete quality pipeline at this HEAD.
next_actions: Reconcile the gating migration into an intentional committed state.
Run the repository lint, coding-standard, PHPStan, PHPUnit, coverage, Panther, and applicable Playwright gates on the reconciled clean tree.
Merge or otherwise finalize the canonical refactor branch after verification.
Create an immutable RC tag only after the verified working tree is clean.
Refresh the Atlas snapshot from the final tagged RC commit.
